proposed.explanation:
ETEL's FY2025 results show a clear and substantial improvement over FY2024. Revenue grew roughly 31% (from 81.68 bn to 106.67 bn EGP), gross profit rose about 47%, and net profit more than doubled (from 10.11 bn to 22.58 bn EGP). Margins expanded meaningfully: gross margin went from ~37% to ~42%, and net margin from ~12% to ~21%. EPS jumped from 4.79 to 11.93 EGP per share. At the current price of 141.95 EGP, the trailing P/E is about 11.9×, which is reasonable for a company growing earnings at this pace. Total equity grew ~39%, suggesting the balance sheet is strengthening alongside the income statement.

For your specific situation – a 5-to-7-year horizon to fund a child's university fees, medium risk tolerance, and a separate emergency fund – holding a fundamentally improving, mid-cap Egyptian company is broadly compatible. You do not need the cash in the near term, and the growth profile supports a multi-year hold.

Important caveats and risks:
• Concentration: your 300 ETEL shares are worth 42,585 EGP out of a 62,585 EGP portfolio (≈68%). This is well above a comfortable single-stock weight. I cannot recommend buying more ETEL because the 50% diversification cap would already be breached, and I have no evidence on alternative listings to diversify into. You may wish to consider, on your own, whether trimming a portion of ETEL and parking the proceeds in cash (or a future diversifying purchase) would reduce single-name risk. The evidence here does not compel a sale, but the concentration is a real risk for a medium-risk-tolerance investor.
• Limited evidence: I only have one year of comparative financials (FY2025 vs FY2024). There is no dividend history, no forward guidance, no sector or competitive context, and no information on the drivers of the profit jump (one-off items vs. recurring growth). A single year of strong results does not guarantee continuation.
• The EPS row is labelled 'L.E. / Share' on the page whose general unit is 'L.E.(000)'. I have treated the values as 11.93 and 4.79 EGP per share (consistent with the row heading and the implied share count of ~1.89 bn). If the page unit were to apply, the P/E calculation would change, but the row heading makes the per-share reading the natural one.

In summary: the fundamentals support continuing to hold your 300 ETEL shares for the 5–7-year window. Keep the 20,000 EGP cash as a buffer. Reassess at the next annual report to confirm the growth is recurring, and consider diversifying if the position remains above ~50% of your portfolio. This is guidance, not a guarantee; equity prices can fall even when fundamentals improve.
